A symmetrising form on the algebra A is a linear map τ : A →R such that
(a) τ(ab) = τ(ba) for all a, b ∈A, that is, τ is a trace function, and
(b) the map bτ : A →HomR(A, R), a 7→(x 7→τ(ax)) is an isomorphism of A-bimodules.
If there exists a symmetrising form on A, we say that A is a symmetric algebra.

blocks.title: Semicontinuity property of Rouquier families
blocks.content: Let m = (mC,j)(C∈A/W )(0⩽j⩽eC−1) be a family of integers and let ϕm : vC,j 7→qmC,j be the corresponding cyclotomic specialisation. The Rouquier families of Hϕm(W) are unions of the Rouquier families associated with the essential hyper- planes that m belongs to and they are minimal with respect to this property. Thanks to the above result, it is enough to do calculations in a ﬁnite number of cases in order to obtain the families of characters for all cyclotomic Hecke algebras, whose number is inﬁnite.

blocks.content:
Decomposition maps and canonical basic sets
Given a cyclotomic Hecke algebra Hϕm(W) and a ring homomorphism θ : q 7→η ∈C \ {0}, we obtain a
semisimplicity criterion and a decomposition map exactly as in §2.4. A canonical basic set with respect
to θ is also deﬁned in the same way.
In [ChJa1], we showed the existence of canonical basic sets with respect to any θ for all cyclotomic
Hecke algebras associated with ﬁnite Coxeter groups, that is, when the weight function L in the deﬁnition
of Hq(W, L) is also allowed to take negative values.
